idiom_name: hand-written encoder/decoder over sqlite3_bind_blob or binary PQexecParams
implementation_notes: ISO C has no serialization facility, so the classic structure survives in full: one encoder walks the struct graph into a growable byte buffer and one decoder parses that layout back with explicit lengths, and the buffer is bound as a BLOB/BYTEA (sqlite3_bind_blob, or a binary parameter to PQexecParams). A schema-driven codec such as protobuf-c or cJSON replaces the hand-written layout when other languages must read the payload or the structs will change often; a table of function pointers per node type is the C stand-in for the serializer class. Never copy a struct image into the column: padding, host byte order and pointer values make it useless elsewhere.
pitfalls: memcpy of a struct stores padding and host byte order: the payload breaks on another compiler, platform or architecture, so encode field by field with a fixed byte order.
A decoder that trusts the lengths inside the blob over-reads on truncated or hostile data; validate every length against the remaining buffer before allocating.
Buffer ownership leaks easily: the encoder's buffer, SQLite's destructor argument (SQLITE_TRANSIENT copies) and decode-side cleanup each need one explicit owner.
